reviewed_sources.title: Effective action for delta potentials: spacetime-dependent inhomogeneities and Casimir self-energy
reviewed_sources.authors: S. A. Franchino-Viñas and F. D. Mazzitelli
reviewed_sources.read_scope: Introduction; section 3.1 form factor and divergent/local/nonlocal split; section 3.2 renormalization conditions; section 4 retarded Wick rotation and pair-production part; conclusions. Original version v2 was pinned and hashed.
reviewed_sources.model_and_limit: Real scalar on flat D-dimensional space with a thin codimension-one delta potential; perturbation theory in spacetime-dependent inhomogeneities around a constant layer. Detailed form factors are for massless D=4. The paper states that the layer's local term depends on the microscopic coupling/renormalization prescription.
reviewed_sources.comparison: Confirms that local divergences and finite nonlocal response must be separated and that the local coefficient belongs to a specified microscopic layer theory. It does not compute our smooth finite 1+1 sec-squared rank-one throat, its strong-cut scaling, or its transmitting exterior. No formula from that model is imported.
reviewed_sources.access_notes: The arXiv HTML was read at equations (33)-(45), renormalization discussion (section 3.2), the Wick-rotated response (equations (56)-(60)) and the conclusions. The local two-point form factor is treated perturbatively in inhomogeneity; the full nonlinear response to our moving throat is not thereby determined.

discovery_leads.scope: Search-result abstract only; not a proof-level review.
discovery_leads.effect: A distinct massive moving-boundary model; it does not resolve the smooth charged throat or joined contact.

discovery_leads.title: Two-dimensional effective action for matter fields coupled to the dilaton
discovery_leads.effect: A potentially relevant covariant heat-kernel effective-action source. Full derivation review remains pending.

novelty_assessment: The universal local/nonlocal split is established and cannot be claimed as new. The explicit free bulk-versus-joined-contact decomposition is a check on this prescribed proper-cut Hamiltonian, not a physical novelty result. Interacting contact, full ultraviolet response, physical matching and complete source exit remain unresolved.
